overview: Both extract energy from glucose, but only one uses oxygen and produces far more ATP.
genZNote: Aerobic respiration is the full-fat energy plan with oxygen. Fermentation is the emergency backup plan when oxygen isn't around.

aspects.label: Oxygen Required?
aspects.valueA: Yes, oxygen is the final electron acceptor.

aspects.label: ATP Yield per Glucose
aspects.valueB: Only 2 ATP per glucose molecule (from glycolysis alone).

aspects.label: End Products
aspects.valueB: Lactic acid (in muscle/animal cells) or ethanol + CO2 (in yeast).

aspects.label: Cellular Location
aspects.valueA: Glycolysis in cytoplasm; Krebs cycle and ETC in mitochondria.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Fermentation's low ATP yield is exactly why intense anaerobic exercise causes rapid muscle fatigue via lactic acid buildup.
overlay.memoryTrick: Aerobic = 'air', needs oxygen, big ATP payout. Fermentation = no air, quick but tiny payout.
overlay.commonMisconception: Fermentation is not simply 'anaerobic respiration' in the strict sense used in some syllabi — some define anaerobic respiration as using an alternate inorganic final electron acceptor, distinct from fermentation.
